When m < n, E can be both an m- and n-cylinder, allowing decomposition into A × X(n) where A ⊂ X₁ × ··· × Xₘ and B ⊂ X₁ × ··· × Xₙ. The relation B = A × X(m+1) × ··· × X(n) follows from 33.C, ensuring consistency in product structure. The set function μ is defined uniquely on such cylinders, preserving finite additivity. The algebra F of finite-dimensional cylinders ensures closure under operations, forming a foundation for extension to infinite products. The key insight is that measurable structures in finite dimensions yield consistent measure-preserving mappings across nested cylinder sets.
